violation_type.title: Prohibited Punishments -  Associated with Food, Naps, or Toilet Training (26 TAC §746.2805(2))
violation_type.short_title: Prohibited Punishments -  Associated with Food, Naps, or Toilet Training
violation_type.typical_finding: During an investigation, it was determined that the method that the caregiver reached and placed the children on the cot was inappropriate.

finding_variants.text: During an investigation, it was determined that the method that the caregiver reached and placed the children on the cot was inappropriate.
Based on DFPS investigation there was a concern that a caregiver pushed a child onto a nap cot.

This standard was found deficient as part of a DFPS investigation. A caregiver did not allow a child to go to the restroom.  This caused the child to soil on themself and made the child clean up the urine.

During the DFPS investigation, there was sufficient evidence to determine that a caregiver disciplined two children by not letting them finish eating their meal after one of the children spilled a cup of milk.
Based on the information gathered food was used as punishment when the child did not want to participate in saying grace.
During investigation, it was determined that the operation withheld food from a child as punishment during a special event in the classroom due to alleged misbehavior.

Prohibited Punishments -  Associated with Food, Naps, or Toilet Training: This standard was found deficient as part of a DFPS investigation.   A caregiver admitted to leaving children sitting on a potty chair for 30 minutes at a time, while potty training.

Prohibited Punishments -  Associated with Food, Naps, or Toilet Training: It was found through investigation that a caregiver would abruptly take food from children if they felt the child was not eating in an appropriate manner. An example would be not using their utensils to put food in their mouth, or taking food apart to eat it.

Prohibited Punishments -  Associated with Food, Naps, or Toilet Training: This standard was evaluated as part of an investigation by the Department of Family and Protective Services and was found to be deficient. The caregiver threw away food before children were done eating, forced a child to use the bathroom, and yanked a mat from underneath a child during nap time. Specific incidents include discarding a child's food for talking too much, forcing bathroom use against their will, and disrupting naps by pulling away mats, causing children to fall. These actions were confirmed by multiple interviews with caregivers who observed these inappropriate disciplinary measures.

occurrences.finding: Prohibited Punishments -  Associated with Food, Naps, or Toilet Training: This standard was reviewed as part of an investigation and found deficient. Per interviews conducted it was determined that in one classroom during naptime, children have gotten in trouble if they did not sleep meaning they are required to put their nap mat by the teacher and sleep or gotten their name written down on the board and not given a reward of candy or a sticker as a result.

Prohibited Punishments -  Associated with Food, Naps, or Toilet Training: Two classrooms were observed making threats to the children in care that they won't have snack time if they don't behave. One placed the child in time out and withheld snack time while the rest of the classroom had snack. In another classroom, the caregiver told the child that they can either eat at the designated chair for snack or could go to time out. The child wanted snack but just wanted a different seat.

Prohibited Punishments -  Associated with Food, Naps, or Toilet Training: The operation used prohibited punishment when they sent a child to "thinking time", which is a time out, for toileting accidents.
Prohibited Punishments -  Associated with Food, Naps, or Toilet Training: A caregiver did not provide a complete snack and lunch to a child as part of a discipline method.

Prohibited Punishments -  Associated with Food, Naps, or Toilet Training: Based on the DFPS investigation, there is sufficient evidence to suggest that a child was inappropriately disciplined when they would not lay down on their nap cot.

Prohibited Punishments -  Associated with Food, Naps, or Toilet Training: Based on information obtained during an investigation, it was found that a caregiver inappropriately restrained a child in care, preventing the child from moving, due to the child not wanting to nap.

occurrences.finding: Prohibited Punishments -  Associated with Food, Naps, or Toilet Training: Based on the information obtained from the DFPS abuse/neglect investigation, it was found that two caregivers were being unnecessarily harsh and cruel in their treatment of children during nap time. Caregivers were observed to pick children up and slam them onto nap mats, pulling children by the arms to force them to lay down straight, kick a child on their legs and back to recenter their bodies on the nap mat, dragging children to the nap mat, and shoving children face down into the nap mat.

Prohibited Punishments -  Associated with Food, Naps, or Toilet Training: This standard was evaluated as part of an investigation and found deficient. A caregiver threatened a child with punishment associated with both toilet training and food.

Prohibited Punishments -  Associated with Food, Naps, or Toilet Training: Interviews were conducted and surveillance tape was reviewed. It was determined that a caregiver placed two 3 yr. old children in the restroom during naptime as a disciplinary measure.    NOTE: The caregiver was terminated.

Prohibited Punishments -  Associated with Food, Naps, or Toilet Training: Based on information obtained during an investigation, it was determined that the snack the child is served is based on the child?s behavior.  Children that are on ?green face? are given what is called a ?super snack.?  Children on ?yellow or red face? are given a different snack.
Prohibited Punishments -  Associated with Food, Naps, or Toilet Training: Caregivers and staff admitted that they give children candy as a reward for toilet training.
